mainText: This is Dose of Good for Sunday, November 15. Here are 5 good news stories. First: 20-year-old Argentine wins at Harvard with a device that guides blind people. Martín Pulitano and his team won HackHarvard, out of 500+ participants, with FEEL: a US$70 prototype that uses AI and touch to signal what's ahead and alongside. They now want blind people to test it. Second: Firefighters swim across a lagoon to save a cat stuck in a quarry wall. The cat was trapped in a crack in a disused quarry in Pernambuco, Brazil. Firefighters Heitor Tabosa and Aniele Gomes swam to the wall and used a rope and carrier to bring it out. It went home safe to its owner. Third: Kenyan defender of elephants and the sea wins conservation award. Raabia Hawa, founder of Ulinzi Africa, won the 2026 Tusk Award. Her group began with anti-poaching patrols for elephants and now fights illegal trawling that was killing turtles. The award brings three years of funding. Fourth: Fortaleza project brings women artisans together on a giant crochet piece. Artesanias em Rede – Mulheres do Mar offers 140 hours of training to 240 women from across the city. It began with mothers who wanted to work from home, and many are now registered artisans. Fifth: Molecule may help prevent diabetes-related vision loss. Researchers at Unifesp and Unesp showed the peptide Ac2-26 stopped neurons dying in human retinal cells and organoids exposed to high glucose and inflammation. Retinopathy affects more than 22% of people with diabetes. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
